thesis: Adjusted operating expansion is real, but unknown legal exposure and funding prevent either advocate from pricing the trade-off. Lower Singapore admissions do not erase group growth; group growth does not settle acquisitions or legal outcomes. Neutral separates operating merit from unquantified entry risk.
strongest_counterexample: Revenue +7%, EBITDA +14% and PATMI excluding exceptional items +30% excluding MFRS129 provide strong growth after removing an important accounting distortion.
invalidation_conditions: Accessible primary legal/audit disclosures establish the actual exposure and a debt-service cash reconciliation shows a positive post-obligation surplus, resolving the central unpriced gates while adjusted growth remains above zero.
Adjusted comparable EBITDA growth at or below zero together with further negative Singapore admissions growth would invalidate the retained operating-expansion counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Underlying Japan appeal and Fortis audit statements/outcomes were inaccessible.
Acquisition-adjusted organic comparisons and Singapore demand drivers.
decisive_factors: Adjusted growth is not exclusively MFRS129-driven.
Price remains below both major averages and low volume limits recovery confirmation.
